_meta.indication: VITRAKVI is indicated for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients with solid tumors that have an NTRK gene fusion without a known acquired resistance mutation, are metastatic or where surgical resection is likely to result in severe morbidity, and have no satisfactory alternative treatments or that have progressed following treatment

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Pooled results from three trials: LOXO-TRK-14001, SCOUT (protocol LOXO-TRK-15003), and NAVIGATE (protocol LOXO-TRK-15002)
pivotal_trials.phase: The three trials correspond to protocols LOXO-TRK-14001 (Phase 1, adult solid tumors), LOXO-TRK 15002 (Phase 2 Basket Study; public name NAVIGATE), and LOXO-TRK 15003 (Phase 1/2, pediatric; public name SCOUT)
pivotal_trials.design: Three multicenter, open-label, single-arm clinical trials
pivotal_trials.population: First 55 pediatric and adult patients with unresectable or metastatic solid tumors with an NTRK gene fusion; most common cancers were salivary gland tumors (22%), soft tissue sarcoma (20%), IFS (13%), and thyroid cancer (9%)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DOR)
pivotal_trials.result: ORR 75% (95% CI: 61%, 85%), including 22% complete response and 53% partial response; among 41 responders, 73% had DOR of at least 6 months and 39% had DOR over a year; median DOR not reached

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%) in order of decreasing frequency were fatigue, nausea, dizziness, vomiting, anemia, increased AST, cough, increased ALT, constipation, and diarrhea. Primary serious risks are hepatotoxicity and neurotoxicity: increased transaminases of any grade in 45% (Grade 3 AST/ALT in 6%); neurologic adverse reactions of any grade in 53% (Grade 3 and 4 in 6% and 0.6%)
target_moa: Kinase inhibitor that inhibits the kinase activities of the tropomyosin receptor kinases TRKA, TRKB, and TRKC; strong scientific rationale that inhibition of TRK causes shrinkage of tumors with NTRK fusions
companion_dx_detail: No FDA-approved test for the detection of NTRK gene fusion is currently available; patients selected based on presence of NTRK gene fusion in tumor specimens (most enrolled by local NGS testing). A PMC was planned to develop a companion diagnostic.

advisory_committee.vote: FDA did not hold an advisory committee meeting because no review issues raised significant public health questions regarding the risk:benefit assessment

description.text: Updated prescribing information with response data from patients with NTRK fusion solid tumors and expanded safety population; labeling changes and fulfillment of postmarketing requirement (no new indication).

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for revisions to the prescribing information (PI) updating the response data from patients with NTRK fusion solid tumors. Additionally, labeling changes were made to Adverse Reactions (Section 6.1) and Pediatric Use (Section 8.4) based on updated safety data expanding the safety population. Warnings and Precautions Section 5.1 was updated to "Central Nervous System Effects" with language to clarify cognitive impairment and other disorders and to Section 5.2 to update "Skeletal Fractures" language. Finally, edits to associated with the previously described edits were made to the Patient Information and Instructions for Use.
